ai.description: *Scincella macrotis* reaches 50 mm SVL. It is brown with dark lateral bands and pale dorsolateral stripes. Distinguishing features include a large, conspicuous ear opening and smooth, cycloid scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Scincella macrotis* is best distinguished by its unusually large, prominent ear opening that lacks the distinct lobules typically found in other Indian ground skinks.
ai.habitat: *Scincella macrotis* inhabits leaf litter in moist deciduous and evergreen forests, typically found at mid-to-high elevations across the Himalayas and Northeast India.
ai.behavior: The Large-eared Ground Skink is primarily diurnal, actively foraging for small invertebrates among leaf litter while relying on rapid movement to escape predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Scincella macrotis* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally from June to August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Scincella macrotis* is found in the Himalayas and Northeast India, ranging from lowlands up to approximately 2,000 meters in elevation.
